# Adversarial dogfood — Phase 26 SM1–SM10 @ bb991a4

**Pin:** `bb991a4` (*Poison structured post-effect ambiguity*).  
**Sources (code over prose):** `spec/phase26/structured-merge.md`; `impl/src/structured-merge.mjs`; `impl/src/worktree.mjs` (stage/finalize/reconcile); `impl/src/coordinator.mjs` (`integrate`, poison, replay); `impl/src/index.mjs` (worktree manager, pins); `impl/test/phase26-structured-merge.test.mjs`; `docs/handoff/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-2026-07-11.md`; Phase 11 integration/replay (`impl/test/phase11-acceptance-integration.test.mjs` AC5/CK9).

## Decision

**No actionable SM1–SM10 implementation defect remains at bb991a4.**

The commit closes the concrete post-effect authority hole: after a successful main fast-forward, `afterSha` / cleanliness failures are tagged `structured_post_effect_inconsistent` + `postEffect: true` (`worktree.mjs` `postEffectMergeError`, `finalizeStructuredIntegration`), and the coordinator records `integration.incomplete` then `_poisonIntegration` instead of `integration.refused` (`coordinator.mjs` integrate catch + `_poisonIntegration`). Pre-effect failures still refuse without moving main; operational success + coordination integration batch remain the only replayable success (`integrationAuthority` + replay `integration.completed` gate). Residual gaps are either explicit non-goals (true semantic merge, live Mergiraf binary, CPG/fingerprint authority) or catastrophic Git subprocess failure modes outside the numbered contract’s testable surface—not ship-blocking SM defects.

| Seam | Verdict |
|------|---------|
| SM1 injected resolver | **Hold** — fixed `mergiraf solve <path>`, `shell: false`, bounded time/output; tests inject executor |
| SM2 main ≠ stage | **Hold** — stage under `.baton/integrate/`; main only FF at finalize |
| SM3 exact identities | **Hold** — before/result/base/stage; parent pair checked at stage + finalize; dirty/advance refuse |
| SM4 fail-closed classify | **Hold** — binary/symlink/markers/fallback/ceilings/unmerged/`diff --check` refuse typed |
| SM5 immutable candidate | **Hold** — two-parent commit only after full resolve + check; not main |
| SM6 fresh verify | **Hold** — distinct verify worktree at `stageSha`; pinned primary; `requireRedGreen: false` |
| SM7 one guarded main update | **Hold** — clean + `HEAD==beforeSha` then `merge --ff-only --no-verify`; hooks disabled |
| SM8 replay/authority | **Hold** — completed only via op log + `completeIntegration` batch; post-effect poisons; incomplete ≠ success |
| SM9 cleanup/retention | **Hold** — stage/verify reaped success/refuse/throw; reconcile sweeps orphans; pin release only on success |
| SM10 semantic boundary | **Hold** — no CPG/fingerprint path in `integrate`; research tombstone in spec only |

## Proposed numbered contract

Operational restatement of SM1–SM10 as enforced by this tree (not a rewrite of the spec):

1. **SM1** Production `MergirafResolver` invokes `execFile(binary, ['solve', relativePath], { shell: false, env: PATH/LANG/LC_ALL only })` with deployment `timeoutMs` / `maxOutputBytes` / `maxFileBytes`. Outcomes: `resolved` only on exit 0 + `solved N conflict` without parse-fallback text; else `parse_fallback` / `unresolved` / `unknown` or typed `structured_tool_*`. Never map textual fallback to structured success.
2. **SM2** `stageStructuredIntegration` requires clean main, pins `beforeSha`, creates detached worktree at `.baton/integrate/<taskId>-<hex>` from `beforeSha`. All merge/resolve/index/commit run there. Main HEAD/index/worktree unchanged until SM7.
3. **SM3** Stage freezes `beforeSha`, full `resultSha`, `mergeBaseSha`, `stageSha`, conflict paths/classes. Refuse: invalid result, result already ancestor of main, dirty main, main ≠ `beforeSha` at finalize, parent pair ≠ `(beforeSha, resultSha)`.
4. **SM4** Clean three-way → `clean_textual`. Each `diff-filter=U` regular text path → isolated temp file + resolver; success class `structured_resolved` only after NUL-free UTF-8, no conflict-marker run of 7+ `<=>|` chars, path realpath stable, `git add`. Binary/delete/escape/fallback/unknown/unmerged/`git diff --check` → typed refuse; stage reaped.
5. **SM5** Candidate is `git commit` of the fully resolved stage with exact two parents; object alone is not acceptance.
6. **SM6** Before main moves: `createVerifyWorktree(taskId-structured-merge, stageSha)` + referee on `task.brief.verification` with `requireRedGreen/Coverage/Mutation: false`. Fail → `structured_verification_failed`, reap stage+verify, retain result pin, main unchanged.
7. **SM7** Only after SM6 accept: recheck clean + `HEAD==beforeSha` + parents, then `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null merge --no-verify --ff-only stageSha`. Success record includes before/result/base/stage/after, classes, resolver identity, verdict. No push/deploy.
8. **SM8** Replayable success iff operational `integration.completed` **and** `coordination.integrationAuthority` (promoted Decision + driver.completed + accepted artifact batch). Asymmetric decision/candidate/resolver report cannot reconstruct success. After Git effect boundary: append `integration.incomplete` + poison (`structured_post_effect_inconsistent`); never `integration.refused`; never silent hard-reset of user HEAD.
9. **SM9** `removeStructuredIntegration` / `removeVerifyWorktree` on every integrate outcome; `reconcile` force-removes all `.baton/integrate/*` (no resume without fresh verdict). Success releases `refs/baton/results/<sha>`; refusal/incomplete retain pin. No stage branch.
10. **SM10** CPG/behavior APIs are not consulted in `integrate`. True semantic merge remains out of scope until an external engine proves false-clean advantage; redirect to structured + fresh verify.

## Red tests and proof

Concrete sequences grounded in source (not worker prose). Codes cite implementation lines by path.

- **Proof:** `structured-merge.mjs` `MergirafResolver.resolve` → `execFile(this.binary, ['solve', relativePath], { shell: false, ... })`; timeout → `structured_tool_timeout`; ENOENT → `structured_tool_unavailable`; fallback regex → `parse_fallback`.
- **Red:** `phase26` *SM1: Mergiraf resolver uses fixed no-shell argv…*; *SM1/SM2: missing resolver…* → `structured_tool_unavailable`, main HEAD/status unchanged, pin retained.
- **Failure sequence (refused correctly):** diverge main+result on `src/value.js` → `integrate({strategy:'structured'})` with `structuredMerge: null` → stage sees conflicts → no resolver → throw → catch reaps stage → main bytes identical.

## Risks and rejection criteria

**Reject a future change if any of the following regress:**

1. Any error after successful main `merge --ff-only` to `stageSha` is recorded as `integration.refused` or leaves the coordinator unpoisoned while HEAD moved (SM8). Tagged `postEffect` / `structured_post_effect_inconsistent` must remain the classification for post-boundary validation failure.
2. Replay sets `task.integration` from operational `integration.completed` without passing `integrationAuthority` (or equivalent atomic Decision+driver+artifact batch).
3. Finalize runs before fresh verify accept, or verify uses the stage worktree / worker worktree instead of a distinct sandbox at `stageSha`.
4. Main is used as merge workspace (conflict files written under main checkout), or ambient `GIT_*` can retarget stage/finalize git.
5. Parse fallback, remaining markers, binary NUL (in or out), escaping realpath swap, or unmerged index can yield `strategy:'structured'` success.
6. Stage/verify directories survive refused/thrown integrate without reconcile, or success drops `refs/baton/results/*` before durable completion while still claiming pin release semantics inconsistently with SM9.
7. CPG/fingerprint (or any advisory) can skip SM6 or advance main.
8. Silent `git reset --hard` of user main to hide post-effect inconsistency.

**Non-reject / explicit non-goals:** absence of host `mergiraf` binary; weak user-pinned verify commands; true semantic merge of incompatible data/control-flow; dangling unreachable stage objects until `git gc`; in-memory poison cleared by process restart without inventing success (operator reconciles Git tip vs authority).

**Residual note (not actionable SM defect):** if `git rev-parse`/`status` itself throws after a successful FF (catastrophic repo breakage), the throw may lack `postEffect` and fall into the refuse branch; that requires Git failure after ref update and is not exercised by the contract’s reds. Production finalize’s normal post-FF checks are already postEffect-tagged. Do not treat this as an open SM1–SM10 item unless a reproducible non-catastrophic sequence appears.
